content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Both citalopram and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Concomitant use should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be considered. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Cobicistat and erythromycin lactobionate mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. Resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. This combination is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 10. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while cortisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Both crizotinib and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darifenacin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and dasatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Both degarelix and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Both desflurane and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Both desipramine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and diltiazem increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Consider an alternative to erythromycin in patients receiving diltiazem. 27. Both dofetilide and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Both donepezil and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Both doxepin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and dronedarone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Both droperidol and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 33. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Both erythromycin lactobionate and entrectinib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
